explanation: The Sahara covers about 9 million km², stretching across North Africa from the Atlantic coast into Egypt and Sudan. Australia covers about 7.7 million km².

claims.text: The Sahara Desert covers about 9 million km².
Australia's total area is about 7.7 million km².
The Sahara stretches across North Africa from the Atlantic coast into Egypt and Sudan.

writerNotes: Self-check (§9.3). Lint: content:check run for the batch and writer; no errors or warnings on this item. Claims: every checkable statement is listed; c1 (number) and c2 (number) are high under the C26 floor, and c3 is standard. Datasets: mledoze-countries: AUS area 7,692,024 (c2). The Sahara's area is in no pinned dataset. Rival test: Australia is a whole continent, so most players assume it is bigger; the desert is bigger. Against the key: published figures for the Sahara run from about 8.6 to 9.4 million km², depending on where its edges are drawn, and even the smallest beats Australia by more than 10%, so the item stores the round 9 million and the 1.1 guard still holds at the low end. Volatility: evergreen, settled geography with no review date; no time words, and nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026. Regional: Both are known everywhere. Style: Oxford spelling, plain hyphens only, straight apostrophes, explanation of 25 words. Myths: every claim screened against content/reference/myths.json; no entry matches. Mystery and encore: nothing of either kind to check in a practice item. External evidence: c1 needs a Tier A or B web result. Seed: 4 (medium): many pick Australia. Counterintuitive: true; the obvious answer is wrong, as the rival test explains, and the explanation defuses it. Doubts: the Sahara's edges are a matter of definition, which is why c1 is approximate.
